Screen checkConfirm in Vanderbilt's Oracle or UKG during a recorded demo: the reason name for a change in working hours; that a regular HCM (not a super-user) sees Our Workforce and this quick action.

1 · Intro

When to use it.

Changing working hours changes FTE, and it can also affect salary, benefits, and PTO.

The process depends on the employee. A non-exempt (hourly) employee's hourly rate generally doesn't change just because the hours change. For an exempt (salaried) employee, an FTE change may also need a salary change. So there are two ways to do it: working hours only, or working hours and salary together.

Use this whenAn employee's scheduled hours or FTE change.

Before you submit

The same four checks on every pay-impacting transaction. Draft: the owner for this area confirms anything marked To confirm.

Attach

  • The approval or agreement for the change Attach

Check

Read every field back against the source document: person, effective date, position, hours, pay, and costing.

  • The right path: Change Working Hours when only hours change; Change Assignment with Salary when salary changes too.
  • Working hours hold the new weekly hours. Standard working hours stay at 40.
  • FTE recalculated as expected (for example, 30 of 40 = 0.75).
  • If salary changed: prorated or the agreed amount entered, with a comment saying what changed and why.

Cutoff

Monthly (exempt) pay: the change must be fully approved by the HCM Transaction Cutoff, the 18th in most months and earlier in December. Check the HR/Payroll Calendar. Pending approvals do not pay. A change still waiting in approvals at the cutoff misses that payroll.

Who does what

  • Who starts it: You.
  • Who approves: To confirm: the approval chain for this transaction.
  • What happens next: Payroll pays the new salary from the effective date.

Watch-outs

  • Change Salary with the reason Change in working hours changes only the salary. The hours need their own transaction, so when both change, use Change Assignment with Salary.
  • An FTE change can affect benefits and PTO, not only pay.
  • Open item: confirm that Change Assignment is the right process when both working hours (FTE) and salary change.
  • Open item: confirm the action reason for a combined working hours and salary change.
  • Open item: confirm when an exempt employee's salary should change because their FTE changes, and when an hours change needs no salary or hourly rate change.
  • Open item: confirm when Payroll Details must be included, and any other differences between exempt and non-exempt employees.
  • Open item: confirm the benefits and PTO impacts of an FTE change to explain in this course.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • Oracle: Redwood employment pages incl. Change Assignment and Change Working Hours (26C) (opens in a new tab)

Q2A non-exempt (hourly) employee drops from 40 to 30 hours, and the hourly rate stays the same. Which action?

HCM Academy job aid · Assignment Changes

Change Working Hours

Use when: An employee's scheduled hours or FTE change. · System: Oracle HCM

  1. Decide which scenario you're in.
    • Working hours only: Change Working Hours
    • Working hours and salary: Change Assignment with Salary
  2. Working hours only: open Employment Info, then the three-dot menu.
  3. Working hours only: enter the effective date and the new hours, then submit.
  4. Working hours and salary: open Employment Info and choose Change Assignment.
  5. Working hours and salary: enter the effective date, then Assignment Change and the action reason.
  6. Working hours and salary: change the hours, then the salary.
  7. Working hours and salary: add comments and documents, then submit.
